title: JRE 2453 - Evan Hafer
guestBio: Evan Hafer is a Special Forces veteran, founder, and executive chairman of Black Rifle Coffee Company, and one of the hosts of the “Black Rifle Coffee Podcast.”
tldr: Evan Hafer shares his journey from Special Forces soldier to building Black Rifle Coffee Company into a multi-million dollar business
Discussion of military culture, what it takes to succeed in Special Forces, and how that shaped Hafer's entrepreneurial mindset
Black Rifle Coffee Company's mission to support veterans and give back to the military community through business
Hafer talks about building a brand that appeals to conservatives and patriots without being preachy about politics
The podcast and content strategy behind Black Rifle Coffee and how they've built a loyal audience
Insights into scaling a business while maintaining company culture and values in a competitive market
recap:
Joe sits down with Evan Hafer, the founder of Black Rifle Coffee Company, for a conversation that touches on everything from military service to building a successful business brand. Hafer is the kind of guy who walks the walk - a genuine Special Forces veteran with real combat experience who decided to start a coffee company with a purpose.

The conversation digs into what it takes to make it in the military at that elite level and how those lessons translated into building a business. Hafer talks about the discipline, the brotherhood, and the uncompromising standards that defined his time in service, and how he brought those same principles to Black Rifle Coffee. The company isn't just about selling coffee. It's about creating a brand that resonates with a specific audience - people who value hard work, sacrifice, and authenticity.

One of the more interesting parts of the discussion is how Hafer has navigated the tricky waters of building a brand that appeals to conservatives and the military community without it feeling forced or preachy. Black Rifle Coffee has managed to create a cultural movement around their products, and Hafer explains the strategy behind that. It's not about jamming politics down people's throats. It's about building something that naturally attracts like-minded people who value the same things.

They also get into the podcast side of things and how content has become a crucial part of Black Rifle's ecosystem. The company has expanded beyond just coffee into a full media and lifestyle brand. Joe and Evan discuss the business of building an audience and keeping people engaged in an oversaturated market. It's clear that Hafer understands that modern business is as much about community building as it is about product quality.

The episode showcases a guy who's genuinely passionate about what he's built and the mission behind it. Whether you're interested in military culture, entrepreneurship, or just appreciate someone who actually practices what they preach, this is a solid conversation.

quotes: You don't just wake up one day and decide to be in Special Forces. It's a commitment to excellence that becomes part of who you are.
Black Rifle Coffee is about creating a brand for people who actually give a shit. Not everyone, just the ones who get it.
Business is a lot like military operations. You need a clear mission, you need people who believe in it, and you need to execute.
The coffee is great, but what really sells is the community and the values behind the brand.
We're not trying to convince anyone of anything. We're just building something for the people who already think like we do.
